FIRST READER'S NOTE, HOW MEERA KNOWS THE NAME 'RAVI': this is accepted, not a defect. 'You're all set, Ravi' is source text. 03-2 asks consent to register his details, and 03-3 shows the 'Yes, please' answer with Meera typing at a monitor turned toward him, so the reader can infer he gave his details. The source forbids showing actual identifying data, so the name cannot be shown being typed.
FIRST READER'S NOTE, 'TODAY'S APPOINTMENT' AFTER 'I'D LIKE TO SEE THE DOCTOR': accepted, not a defect. Both lines are verbatim source. 'Appointment' reads naturally as the visit being booked now.

FIRST READER'S NOTE, THE CONSULTATION HAS NO OUTCOME: accepted, not a defect. The source requires 'no diagnosis or medical advice' and 'without giving specific treatment advice', and ends the scene with 'decide the right next steps together'. Page 5 then follows the source's 'Ravi leaves, reassured'. 04-4 shows Ravi relaxed and nodding, so the reader is not left hanging.

FIRST READER'S NOTE, PAGE 6 NEW CHARACTERS AND THE UNLABELLED TRAIN PANEL 06-1: accepted, not a defect. The source introduces the specialist, partner and child only as symbolic vision figures, and asks for the vision label on panels 2 and 3. Panel 1 in the source is a 'simple train-window transition' with the conditional caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown'. The word 'may' marks it as hypothetical, and it shows no product feature that would need the vision label. Ravi's same green shirt in 06-1 and 06-3 follows the costume plan and keeps him recognisable. The partner's mustard kurta, wavy loose hair and mole set her apart from Ananya and Meera.

FIRST READER'S NOTE, CHAIR AND HAIR DRIFT: real but minor, and I am not counting them as defects. Page 1 waiting chairs are grey perforated metal in 01-1 and 01-2 but blue padded in 01-3. Page 3 chairs are teal, which can read as the later, refitted reception. Ravi's consultation chair has wooden arms in 04-1, black plastic arms in 04-2 and blue/wood arms in 04-4. Ananya's bun looks looser in 02-4 and 06-4. None of these changes the setting, the character's identity or the reading.

EXTRA AMBIGUITY I FOUND: in 03-1 a navy reception phone lies on the desk. 03-2 shows Ravi holding a similar dark-blue phone, so a reader may take it for his. The script records it as the reception's own phone, it does not affect comprehension, and I am not counting it as a defect.
WORDING: 'Our time belongs with patients' is slightly unidiomatic, but it is verbatim source and should stay.

Reading the unnumbered final pages, each page reads in left-to-right rows: the wide top panel first, then the middle row left then right, then the bottom wide panel. Page 1 runs top wide, then lower left, then lower right.
01-2: the first balloon (top-left, higher) is read before the second (right, lower). Both are Meera's, nothing sits between them, and no reply is skipped.

02-1 and 02-3: the white narration box or balloon is read first and the teal label box second. On 02-1 the label is level at the top right; on 02-3 it sits at the bottom. The different box styles keep the labels from being read as speech.
05-2: Ravi's question balloon at the top left is read before the HEALTH label at the bottom left. 05-3 answers him directly from the next panel to the right.

06-2 and 06-3: the WELBUK VISION label at the top left is read before the caption under it or below it. 06-4: the product label at the top right is read before the final caption at the bottom left. This matches the script order, because the label is higher on the page.
Every question gets its answer in the next balloon: 03-1 to 03-2, 03-2 to 03-3, 04-1 to 04-2, 05-2 to 05-3. I found no case where nearby but non-consecutive balloons pull the eye past a reply.

transitions.observation: Same clinic and morning. The exterior shows the reception desk and phone through the glass, and the cut goes inside to the same desk with paper registers and a ringing phone.
Same moment. Meera is still on the phone writing in the register, small in the background, while Ananya watches with a hand at her chin and gives her resolve line.
Ananya's 'Let's make the rest simpler' leads into the onboarding caption on the next page. A sunset window and a laptop show the time and place change, with the same coat and bun.
Same office at sunset. The cut goes from over-the-shoulder typing to a front view of Ananya at the same laptop with a hand at her chin.
Meera's 'And our team...' continues Ananya's line. Same sunset window and desk with the open laptop, so Meera has joined in the office.
Two-shot of the same two women: Ananya seated at the laptop, Meera standing with the same calendar-screen phone. The coordination line wraps up the scene.
Page turn to daylight at a tidier reception with a computer instead of ledgers, showing the change after onboarding. 'Good morning' and a new arrival confirm a later morning.
Reverse over-the-shoulder shot across the same desk and monitor. Ravi's green shirt is in the left foreground and Meera faces us. The axis flip reads clearly from costumes and the desk.
The consent question gets the answer 'Yes, please'. Ravi stays left and Meera right, she types, and his phone now lies on the desk.
Registration is done. Same left/right staging, Meera gestures toward the teal waiting chairs, and Ravi turns with his hand on his bag strap.
Being told to take a seat leads to being called in. The new room (desk, window, plant, closed laptop) and the same costumes show it is the same visit. The bag is now on the floor.
'Tell me what brings you in' is answered by 'I've been feeling tired lately'. Ananya's head with bun and gold stud is in the left foreground, so she stays left and Ravi right.
Silent listening reaction. Ravi's head is in the right foreground and Ananya listens with folded hands. The caption gives the theme without speech.
The listening beat resolves into the shared next-steps line. Same two-shot axis, Ravi nods, and his bag is still on the floor.
Page turn back to reception (teal chairs, monitor, counter) with the bag back on his shoulder. Meera points at his phone, which leads into the app topic.
Close-up of the phone Meera pointed at, now held toward the reader with calendar and heart icons. Ravi's question follows Meera's explanation.
'So I can...?' is answered by 'That's the idea'. Meera faces right toward Ravi's back, and his phone screen faces her, keeping Meera left and Ravi right.
Time skip after the walkthrough to the clinic exterior (glass doors, teal awning as on page 1). Ravi waves, phone in hand, and the two staff wave back.
Ravi walking away leads to Ravi on a train past a city skyline, in the same shirt and with the same bag and phone. 'Tomorrow... may' marks it as a hypothetical step forward.
'Beyond our hometown' leads into the labelled WELBUK VISION panel: another city's clinic and specialist, with dotted lines linking clinics, in a lighter vignette.
Same vision label and vignette, widening from the clinic network to Ravi's family with a wellness tablet.
The vignette and label end, and the scene returns to the full-colour present at the familiar clinic entrance. The three main characters pose with the product label and the final caption.

readingReview.comparison: The first reader found the reading order and tails clear on every page, and this comparison confirms it: the panel order and balloon order I predicted match the script on all 23 panels. The first reader's concerns are all source choices, not defects: the name 'Ravi', 'today's appointment', the consultation without an outcome (required by the source's no-advice rule), the new vision characters and the unlabelled 06-1 (the source labels only panels 2 and 3, and 06-1 is the conditional train transition). The chair and hair drift is real but minor and does not affect reading or identity. No unresolved defect remains.
